If the solution can be plain JavaScript that'd be great, but jQuery will work too. In a DOM structure like below I'm trying to take only the direct descendant of .root) that possess the child class and hide it with style.display('none').

<div class="root">
 <div class="element">text</div>
 <div class="child">child 1</div>
 <div class="element">child 1's text</div>
 <div class="child">child of child 1</div>
 <div class="child">child 2</div>
 <!--possibly more .child nodes-->
</div>

Earlier in the script I've defined a variable thisChildren. How can I assign it and then iterate over it to "collapse" the .child nodes?

Thanks!
Hiding each element returned by querySelectorAll('div.child')

So for the solution I decided to sacrifice just working with the top-level children, and set thisChildren = document.querySelector('div.child'). Then the code iterated over every element in the thisChildren array, running thisChildren[i].classList.add('hidden'). I had .hidden defined as display: none in CSS. It wouldn't matter if the nested children had the hidden class since they were already not shown.

$('.root > .child').parent().each( function(index, elem) { $(elem).css('display', 'none'); })

This is why jquery rocks.
Oh, so that's the jQuery solution. I'm surprised this got dug up after a month xD
